faqs.question: What does the Fungal Stain test - CSF measure?
faqs.answer: This test detects the presence of fungal organisms in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) using KOH and Calcofluor White stains.

faqs.question: Why is the Fungal Stain test - CSF done?
faqs.answer: • To diagnose fungal infections in the central nervous system • To identify the type of fungus causing the infection • To guide appropriate treatment options • To monitor the effectiveness of antifungal therapy

faqs.question: When is the Fungal Stain test - CSF recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: This test may be recommended if you have • symptoms suggestive of a fungal infection in the central nervous system, such as severe headaches, fever, confusion, or neck stiffness, • a compromised immune system that increases the risk of developing opportunistic fungal infections • a history of systemic fungal infections, or • a suspected fungal meningitis or encephalitis.

faqs.question: What if the results of the Fungal Stain test - CSF are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results suggest the presence of fungal organisms and can indicate a fungal infection in the central nervous system.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Fungal Stain test - CSF?
faqs.answer: During this test, a small amount of CSF will be collected through a sterile procedure. The CSF sample will be sent to the laboratory for processing.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Fungal Stain Test - CSF?
faqs.answer: • Ensure that the specimen is properly collected and stored in a sterile leak-proof container. • Inform your doctor if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with the Fungal Stain Test - CSF?
faqs.answer: • CSF Culture: This test helps in identifying the specific type of fungus causing the infection. • Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR): PCR testing can detect fungal DNA in the CSF, aiding in the diagnosis of fungal infections.

faqs.question: What is Fungal Stain By KOH & Calcofluor White Stain - CSF also known as?
What is fungal meningitis or encephalitis?
faqs.answer: Fungal meningitis or encephalitis is a condition characterised by inflammation of the meninges (protective membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord) or the brain itself, caused by fungal infections. It can lead to severe neurological symptoms and requires prompt diagnosis and treatment.
